items.text: Finding the centreofgravity ofa sheetof card

items.label: text
items.text: Ifyou have a sheetof card orany other uniform material thenfinding its centre of as shown in Figure 5.8.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 5.8The centre of gravity for these three regular shapes is where the axes of symmetry cross. An axis of symmetry can be found using aplane mirror. lf you place a plane mirror along one of the dotted lines in any of the above shapes,the reflection in the miror looks exacty like the original.

items.label: text
items.text: A simple see-saw is a uniform beam (plank)pivoted in the middle.The centre of gravity of a uniformbeam isin the middle,so the see-sawispivoted through its centre of gravity.When an object isnotpivoted through its centre of gravity the weight of the object willproduce a turning effect.This is shown in Figure 5.9.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 5.9 The weight of the beam causes a clockwise tunning effect about the pivot.

items.text: The weight of the ruler actsvertically through the centreof gravity of the rule.As theruleris uniform the centreofgravityisat the 50 cm mark.
